title: Nested If Statements
story: You wake up and need to decide what to wear. First question: is it cold outside? If yes, do you need a heavy coat or just a jacket? If no, is it sunny enough for shorts? Decisions inside decisions � that's what nested ifs are for!
why: Nested conditions let programs handle complex, multi-step decisions � from game AI to recommendation engines to form validation.
analogy: Nested ifs are like a choose-your-own-adventure book � each decision leads to a new set of choices.
try_it: Create a two-level decision tree about your evening plans. First check if you have homework. If yes, check the subject. If no, check if it's nice outside. Print different activities for each path!
tips: Keep nesting to 2-3 levels deep � any deeper and the code gets hard to read. Consider using `elif` instead.
Indent each inner block by the same amount � consistency makes nested code readable!
When both conditions must be true, `&&` can sometimes replace nesting: `if a && b` instead of two nested ifs
common_mistakes: Getting lost in curly braces � count them! Every `{` needs a matching `}`. If the count is off, the compiler gets confused.
Putting code in the wrong block because of incorrect indentation � the code after an if only runs if the condition is true
